## Results

1. Transcript

Iron pills only absorb 10 to 15%. The rest just passes through you. I tracked my ferritin for 18 months. Ferrosisulfate, bisglycinate, floridax, thorn. My number went from 11 to 13 in a year and a half. Here's the part nobody told me. Your gut has a fixed number of DMT1 receptors. They're the doors that let iron into your bloodstream. Once they're full, that's it. You can take a 65 milligram pill. You can take a 150 milligram pill. Doesn't matter. The doors don't change. And there's a second trap. Higher doses spike a hormone called heptadone, which blocks absorption for 24 to 48 hours after you take them. So that big mega dose iron pill is actually absorbing less than a small one. The only fix is to skip the gut entirely. Caviar melt dissolves on your tongue in 30 seconds. The iron goes through your mouth tissue straight into the blood. Different pathway, different rules. Tap the link, read the science, decide for yourself.

2. Transcript

I just realized I've been lied to about iron pills for two years. My ferricin went from 14 to 16. That's it. 16. After 10 different bottles, after every protocol, after timing my vitamin C and skipping clausium and alternating days, then I found this out. Your gut only absorbs 10 to 15% of any iron pill you swallow. There's a transport protein in your intestine called DMT1. There's only so many of them. Once they're full, the rest of the iron just leaves right through you. The pill companies know this. They just keep selling you higher doses. I switched to a strip that dissolves on my tongue, goes through my mouth tissue, straight into the bloodstream. No gut, no sealing. Cave melt.

I'm a runner. For three months, my legs felt like concrete, and my easy pace felt like a sprint. My heart rate was sky high. Everyone said I was overtraining. They were wrong. I thought I was washed up. I felt like a fraud at my own sport. So I checked my ferritin. My doctor said it was normal. But a runner needs 50. Mine was 18. Iron pills always wrecked my stomach, so I'd quit by week two. Then I found a raspberry strip that melts on your tongue. Gentle, no stomach issues, so I finally kept taking it. Eight weeks later, I retested. 18 to 62. My easy runs felt easy again. Talking through my long run instead of gasping, I got myself back. If your pace vanished, check your ferritin. Links below.
